newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FOOD INDUSTRY COMPETITIVENESS SHOULD RISE -PM.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FOOD INDUSTRY COMPETITIVENESS SHOULD RISE -PM.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Tuesday that more work was needed to further boost the competitiveness of the Finnish food industry.
"Work must continue to improve the competitiveness of the food industry and agriculture," Lipponen said in the text of prepared speech.
"In the future, too, it will be essential to improve the competitiveness of Finnish agriculture," he said.
In the year 2000, the European Union's agricultural policy would have to be revised due to World Trade Organisation requirements.
"This means that producer prices will fall and that must be partly compensated with direct income support," Lipponen said.

From Finland's point of view it would be acceptable to reduce agricultural support to areas where production is feasible without support and allocate the support to where it is actually really necessary, he said.
